description:
We are a team of two passionate and curious girls who are a strongly interested in science, technology, and discovering the world beyond what we already know. We believe that great ideas begin with curiosity, creativity, and the courage to approach challenges from different perspectives.

Ready to shape the world!
summary:
School-age children who are interested in space generally focus their attention on active satellites that are still carrying out their missions. However, as you can imagine, it is difficult to explain the stories and histories of satellites that have completed their missions, the heroes of the past who have successfully contributed to the foundations of today’s achievements, to children aged 7–12 through scientific information alone.

Through this project, we aimed to expand children’s knowledge of former satellites by writing this story. Our project supports the aims of the NASA Space Apps Challenge we chose, as the Challenge itself aims to make information accessible to children in this age group in an easy and enjoyable way, while still maintaining its educational value. This is where the importance of our project comes into play.

Our project is important because it does more than teach children the launch dates, mission durations, and scientific achievements of former satellites. By presenting satellites as story characters, it shares their experiences, memories, and emotions with children, allowing them to connect with the stories while gaining scientific knowledge.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Where Silence Becomes a Story is an illustrated, interactive digital storybook designed for school-age children (ages 9–13) and space enthusiasts. Written from a warm, first-person perspective, the story follows ITUpSAT1—Türkiye’s first locally built CubeSat—as it travels to the Graveyard Orbit after completing its mission. There, it meets real retired spacecraft from around the world, including NASA’s EO-1, ASTERIA, and Vanguard 1, and  Russia’s Spektr-R. Through friendly dialogue these silent explorers share their real launch histories thier own stories , scientific discoveries, and memories of Earth.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
While young students often hear about active space missions, the stories of retired and forgottten spacecraft drifting silently above us remain largely unknown. Our project connects  the gap between complex orbital mechanics and child friendly storytelling. By giving real satellites human-like feelings, curiosity, and the sense of friendship, we aim to spark empathy, inspire future engineers, and show how international space missions share a common sky.

Tools & Software Used:
To create a, visually engaging reading experience, we used Canva for visual design, layout, and storybook illustration, alongside official mission archives from NASA and ESA eoPortal to ensure 100% scientific accuracy in every single detail.

Creativity & Key Considerations:
Instead of presenting cold technical facts or a traditional timeline, we imaged real spacecraft—turning historical data into a bedtime-style adventure that  connects the sleeping cities on Earth with the quiet satellites in orbit. In developing the narrative, we carefully balanced age-appropriate language (for 9–13-year-olds), and strict historical accuracy, ensuring that every launch date, mission duration, and hometown detail reflects the reality.
